issues.legal_issue: A will is valid when the propounder proves its execution and the testator’s capacity, and the evidence satisfactorily dispels the suspicious circumstances surrounding it.
material_facts: The deceased had testamentary capacity and was in good health when the will was said to have been made.
The scribe and two attesting witnesses testified that the deceased dictated the will, read it, signed it in their presence, and that they then attested it.
The court found the scribe and attesting witnesses reliable and found no adequate basis to conclude that they had colluded to fabricate the will.
The beneficiaries had close connections with the deceased, and the dispositions were found neither unnatural nor unjust in light of their relationships and circumstances.
The will’s signature had been challenged, but the High Court preferred the defendants’ handwriting expert, and the Supreme Court found no reason to disagree with that assessment.
issues.conclusion: The propounder proved the will; the High Court was correct to find it genuine and valid, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: The propounder bears the burden of proving a will. If there are no suspicious circumstances, proof of testamentary capacity and the testator’s signature as required by law is sufficient; if suspicious circumstances exist, the propounder must explain them to the court’s satisfaction. Once they are removed, the will must be given effect even if it cuts off near relatives. The Court relied on Shashi Kumar v. Subodh Kumar.

rule.if: will_validity_appeal and testator_capacity_established and execution_supported_by_scribe_and_attesting_witnesses and witnesses_found_reliable and signature_supported_by_expert_and_court_assessment and dispositions_reasonable_in_context

predicates.will_validity_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal in which the validity of a propounded will is disputed.
predicates.testator_capacity_established: The evidence establishes that the testator had the capacity to make the will.
predicates.execution_supported_by_scribe_and_attest: The scribe and attesting witnesses testify to the testator’s execution of the will and its attestation.
predicates.witnesses_found_reliable: The court finds the witnesses to the will reliable and finds no adequate evidence that they colluded to fabricate it.
predicates.signature_supported_by_expert_and_court_: The expert and other evidence, considered by the court, support the conclusion that the challenged signature is the testator’s.
predicates.dispositions_reasonable_in_context: The dispositions are consistent with the testator’s relationships and circumstances and are not found unnatural or unjust.

issues.definition: When an appeal disputes a will’s validity, the will is proved if the testator had capacity, execution and signature are supported by reliable evidence, and the dispositions are reasonable in context.
